snapshot.title: SSC REVISION: History & Geography (Days 43–48)
snapshot.exam_hook: ⚡ SSC GK Hook: 1526: Panipat 1. 1885: INC. K2: Highest India. Venus: Morning Star. Stratosphere: Ozone. 1942: Quit India. ⚡ v12 Stamina Hook: 60-min Sprint active.

quick_notes.title: History Timeline Recap
quick_notes.detail: IVC (Lothal). Buddha (Sarnath). Panipat 1 (1526). Akbar (Sikri). 1857 (Canning). INC (1885). Dandi (1930). Quit India (1942).
quick_notes.explanation: The Indus Valley Civilization, or IVC, had a major port city called Lothal. The Buddha gave his first sermon at Sarnath. The First Battle of Panipat in 1526 led to the start of the Mughal Empire. Emperor Akbar built his capital at Fatehpur Sikri, often called Sikri. In 1857, a large uprising against British rule broke out while Lord Canning was the Governor-General. The Indian National Congress, or INC, was founded in 1885 as a political group. Mahatma Gandhi led the Dandi March in 1930 to protest the salt tax. The Quit India movement in 1942 demanded an end to British rule immediately.

quick_notes.title: Geography Superlatives Recap
quick_notes.detail: Atmosphere (Strato: Ozone). Crust (Sial). K2 (Highest India). Gujarat (Coast). Venus (Morning Star). Mariana (Deepest).
quick_notes.explanation: The Earth's atmosphere has layers; the stratosphere is the layer that contains the ozone layer, which protects us from harmful sunlight. The Earth's crust includes the sial layer, meaning it is made of silica and aluminum, and this forms the continents. K2 is the name of the highest mountain peak located within India. Gujarat is the Indian state with the longest coastline, meaning it has the most shore along the sea. Venus is the planet that appears very bright in the morning sky and is therefore called the Morning Star. The Mariana Trench is the deepest known part of any ocean on Earth.

quick_notes.title: Boundary & Peak Recap
quick_notes.detail: Radcliffe (Pak), McMahon (China), Durand (Afghan). Everest (Asia), Kilimanjaro (Africa), Denali (N.America).
quick_notes.explanation: The Radcliffe Line is the border between India and Pakistan, drawn in 1947 by a British lawyer named Sir Cyril Radcliffe. The McMahon Line is the border between India and China, established by a 1914 agreement between British India and Tibet. The Durand Line is the border between Pakistan and Afghanistan, created in 1893 by British diplomat Sir Mortimer Durand. Mount Everest, located in Asia, is the highest mountain in the world. Mount Kilimanjaro, found in Africa, is the highest peak on that continent. Denali, located in North America, is the highest mountain in that continent.

quick_notes.title: River & Grassland Recap
quick_notes.explanation: The Ganga River is also known as the Padma in Bangladesh, and the Brahmaputra River is called the Tsangpo in Tibet before it enters India. Grasslands are large, open areas covered mostly with grass rather than trees. The Prairies are grasslands found in the USA, the Steppes are grasslands found across Eurasia (Europe and Asia), and the Downs are grasslands found in Australia.

quick_notes.title: Mughal & Sultanate Recap
quick_notes.explanation: The Delhi Sultanate began with Qutb-ud-din Aibak, who was a slave of Muhammad Ghori and founded the Slave Dynasty, so remember "Aibak (Slave)" to connect him to that dynasty. Alauddin Khilji, a later Sultan, is famous for controlling the prices of goods in the market through strict economic regulations, which is why you can recall "Khilji (Market)". During the Mughal Empire, Emperor Akbar abolished the jizya, which was a special tax that non-Muslims had to pay, so "Akbar (Jizya)" means he removed that tax. In contrast, Emperor Aurangzeb reimposed the jizya and was known as "Zinda Pir," which means "living saint" in Persian, because of his very strict and pious Muslim lifestyle.

lesson_intro: Today we consolidate the 'Core GK' block. You have mastered the Ancient, Medieval, and Modern facts of India, along with the physical and world geography. In SSC, GK is the 'Time Saver'. If you know the fact, it takes 2 seconds. Today, we drill the years, the kings, and the locations. If you see '1526', you say 'Panipat'. If you see 'Nathula', you say 'Sikkim'. Let's lock in the GK marks today.
